pick.headline: Baker and Tariq Aziz meet in Geneva
pick.summary: On January 9, 1991, US Secretary of State James Baker and Iraqi Foreign Minister Tariq Aziz met in Geneva for over six hours; Aziz refused to accept a letter from President Bush to Saddam Hussein.
pick.significance: It was the last high-level attempt to avert war before the UN's January 15 deadline for Iraq to leave Kuwait.
pick.fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of January 9, 1991, listed, under its Iraq heading, a run of Baghdad radio and INA items on the "'Aziz-Baker Talks in Geneva": Aziz arriving "ready for 'positive' talks", meeting the Swiss foreign minister, and the first and second rounds of talks.

alternates.headline: Bosnian Serbs proclaim their own republic
alternates.summary: On January 9, 1992, Bosnian Serb leaders proclaimed a Serb republic within Bosnia-Hercegovina.
alternates.significance: The proclamation prefigured the partition of Bosnia and the war that began three months later.
